page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor with 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration utilizes a shared allocation model with one thread per core. The system is equipped with 480.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance includes two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs with a combined total of 384 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations. The server achieved top-tier results in Passmark CPU score, Passmark CPU physics, and Passmark database operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and large-block read-only memory bandwidth also placed in the top-tier category. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng, is average, reflecting the 2.0 GHz clock speed and shared CPU allocation. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and large-block write memory bandwidth remain strong, placing in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds for small LLM inference models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density, combining massive GPU memory with a substantial system RAM footprint. The primary hardware tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions. Given the dual NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs and 384 GB of VRAM, this server is highly optimized for deep learning, large language model inference, parallel scientific computing, and high-throughput database operations.
